hook_text: The kettle in your kitchen might be powered by a lump of coal burned 200 kilometres away. Here's how.
clip_script: Ogies, Mpumalanga. Coal rides a conveyor belt into the power station. Ground to powder, blown into a furnace. Whoosh! The heat boils water into steam. Steam blasts a turbine, spinning 3000 times a minute. The turbine turns a generator: a giant magnet spinning in copper coils. Electricity! Up the pylons, through transformers, into your kitchen. Chemical, heat, movement, electrical.
visual_style: Whiteboard flow from a coal heap to a furnace, boiler, turbine, generator, pylons and a house, with energy labels on each arrow.
mood: Powerful and impressive, like a giant machine waking up.
pacing: One stage per beat, speeding up like the turbine.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the electricity meter at your home.
